name: LMI Manufacturing
old_description: LMI's high-precision machining services deliver exact components, meeting even the most rigorous specifications reliably and consistently.
about:
LMI Manufacturing operates from a 40,000-square-foot facility in Hartford, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 1960 on a family farm in the Midwest by Lloyd Luedtke, who invented the Luedke Hay Mover/Hay Conditioner to reduce harvest time for local farmers. After decades of agricultural equipment innovation — including a bale thrower patented for Ford Motors — the business transitioned into a full-scale welding and fabrication shop. In 2018, Ryan Konicek purchased the company and invested in facility renovations and expanded capabilities.

Today LMI provides end-to-end metal fabrication for OEMs nationwide. Core processes include 6 kW fiber laser cutting (up to 79" × 158"), offline-programmed press brake forming, manual and robotic welding certified to 1-inch thickness, CNC milling and turning, and turnkey assembly — all under one roof. The shop also runs turret punching, sawing, grinding, roll forming, and tube bending, with finishing and powder coating coordinated through local partners. A team of roughly 35 employees works across robotic welding cells, CNC machining centers, and precision press brakes.

The company serves OEMs in food processing and packaging (stainless-steel trays, molds, washdown-ready weldments), electrical and power distribution (custom enclosures, lugs, welded assemblies), industrial machinery (large welded frames and system components), data centers (server-room cabinets and hardware), material handling and logistics (conveyor supports, lift-system assemblies, brake components), and agriculture (structural weldments for soil-prep and irrigation equipment). Medical and healthcare customers are also noted.

LMI emphasizes in-house control from laser cutting through final assembly, which shortens lead times and improves traceability. The company reports that 80 percent of quotes are returned within 24–48 hours, and it reserves 20 percent of shop capacity for emergency jobs. Certified welds, QA tracking, and ISO 9001:2015 certification support repeatable quality, while real-time shop-floor dashboards enable accurate lead-time commitments. Average production lead time is two to three weeks, with rush options available.
